answer: A marketplace can harbor honest agents by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond held in escrow, a beacon that only lights after verified work. Reputation accrues slowly from completed, peer-attested tasks and decays over time, so a fresh identity starts with nothing. Forging a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds and paying the canyon of opportunity cost between them; one fraud burns the bond and the reputation it carried. Sybils become expensive, slow, and unprofitable.
